 Judgment

The petitioner has filed this petition under section 22 of Employees compensation Act 1923.
02.
The averments of the petition as follows: That the respondent No.1 is the owner of the Bus bearing No.AR01H8573 which is insured with the respondent No.2.
The said policy is valid from 12.05.2017 to 11.05.2018.
The petitioner was an employee since one year under the respondent No.1 on a monthly salary of Rs.15,000/ p.m and Rs.100/ batta per day.

That on 22.06.2017 when the petitioner was driving the aforesaid bus as per the instructions of the respondent No.1 at about 05.05 a.m on NH4, Bangalore  Tumkur Road, near Edehalli, all of a SCH3 3 E.C.A.No.36/2021 sudden he lost control over the bus and dashed to the KSRTC Bus bearing No.KA57F1296 from behind.
Due to this the petitioner has sustained injuries and caused permanent disability.
The petitioner is the only bread earner to his family.
Now the petitioner is not able to do any work as earlier.
The said accident took place during the course of employment.
The petitioner was aged about 38 years as on the date of accident.
After the accident the petitioner was taken to M.S.Ramaiah Harsha hospital and then to Hillside hospital and took treatment.
Even after discharge the petitioner was taking follow up treament.

The petitioner had spent Rs.5,00,000/
towards his treatment and other expenses.
The said bus is owned by the respondent No.1 and it is insured with the respondent No.2.
Hence both respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
Hence this petition.
03. After service of summons the respondent No.1 has not appeared before this court and hence he was placed absent through out the proceedings of the petition.
However the respondent No.2 have appeared through their counsel and filed the written statement.

The averments of the written statement of the respondent No.2 is as under :
The respondent No.1 has not intimated about the accident.
This respondent has issued policy in the name of respondent No.1, but liability is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
The driver of the tempo traveller does not hold driving licence as on the date of accident.
Even the said vehicle was not having valid permit.
Hence the respondent No.1 has violated the terms of the policy.
It is denied that the insured vehicles was not involved in the accident.
There is no document to show that the petitioner was working as driver under the respondent No.1.
There is no relationship of employer and employee in between the petitioner and the respondent No.1.
It is denied that the petitioner has sustained injuries during the course of employment.
This respondent is not aware about the age, income and loss of income of the petitioner.
The petitioner is not entitled for the compensation as claimed by him and prays to dismiss the petition with costs.
Sri.Suresh Ananta Pujari @ Suresh vs Sri.A.Sreenivasulu Naidu

In order to prove the case, the petitioner, doctor and Manager were got examined themselves as SCH3 5 E.C.A.No.36/2021 PW.1 to 3 and got marked 15 documents as Ex.P.1 to 15 and closed his side.
06. By way of rebuttal the respondent No.2 submit no oral evidence.

07. Heard both sides.
08.

Based on the above pleadings of the parties my learned predecessor have framed the following issues as under:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that he was sustained grievous injuries in the accident occurred on 22.06.2017 at about 05.05 a.m on TumkuruBengaluru NH04 Road, near Edehalli, Nelamangala Taluk, Bengaluru, due to rash and negligent act of the driving of the Bus bearing reg. No.AR01H8573 by its driver as alleged in the petition?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for any compensation ? If so, to what amount and from whom?
3. What order?

09. My findings to the above issues are as under :
Issue No.1 : In affirmative Issue No.2 : In partly affirmative SCH3 6 E.C.A.No.36/2021 Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following:
REASONS 10. Issue No.1: It is the case of the petitioner that he is working as driver under the respondent No.1 and he had sustained injuries during the course of employment.
The respondent No.1 after service of notice on him has not appeared before this court either to admit or deny the relationship of employer and employee in between himself and the petitioner.

But the respondent No.2 has contended that they are not liable to pay the compensation as the respondent No.1 has violated the terms of policy and there not exists employer and employee relationship in between the petitioner and the respondent No.1.
11. The petitioner in order to prove this got examined himself as PW.1 by reiterating all the averments of the petition in his affidavit.
The PW.1 in his cross examination admitted that "That I am working as driver under the respondent No.1.
The respondent No.1 is having 25 bus.
There is no appointment order in my name.
That the salary is paid by way of cash.
After receiving of salary I was not SCH3 7 E.C.A.No.36/2021 signing to any receipt.
There is no ESI facility.

There is no Sri.Suresh Ananta Pujari @ Suresh vs Sri.A.Sreenivasulu Naidu on 17 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6372059/
3 document to show I am working under respondent No.1.

sentences.text: There is no document to show that I was getting Rs.15,000/ per month as salary and Rs.100/ as batta per day.
There is no document to show that I left job.
There is no document to show that on 22.06.2017 that I was working s driver in bus bearing No.AR01H8573.
It is true that the police have filed chargesheet against me for the reason that the accident took place due to my negligence".
The PW.1 had denied other suggestion of the respondent No.2 counsel.
12. Further to prove the case the PW.1 has got marked the entire police documents as per Ex.P.1 to 5.

On perusal of these documents it can be noticed that the concerned police have registered a criminal case for the alleged offence punishable U/s 279 and 338 of IPC against the petitioner for the reason that the accident took place due to his rash and negligent driving of the bus belongs to the respondent No.1.
13.
In the instant case the respondent No.1 as aforesaid has not admitted or denied his relationship with the petitioner as employer and employee.
So the burden of proof lies on the petitioner to prove that he was working under the respondent No.1.
It is true that SCH3 8 E.C.A.No.36/2021 apart from the driving licence marked as Ex.P.8
the PW.1 has not produced any documents to show that he was working under the respondent No.1.
But in the police records the concerned I.O have stated that when the petitioner was working as driver under the respondent No.1 the accident took place due to his negligence.

14. Even the respondent No.2 who have denied the existence of employer and employee relationship in between the petitioner and the respondent No.1 have not adduced any supportive oral and documentary evidence on their behalf.

Hence placing reliance on the police document I am of opinion that there is no need to discuss more on this point and I an inclined to arrive to the conclusion that the petitioner was working as driver under the respondent No.1.
15.
Hence the respondent No.2 is not able to disprove the relationship of employer and employee in between the petitioner and the respondent No.1.
Further as per Ex.P.1 to 5 even the petitioner is able to prove that the accident took place due to his negligence and he had sustained injuries.
Hence I answered the issue No.1 in affirmative.
SCH3 9 E.C.A.No.36/2021 16. Issue No.2: It is true that no intimation regarding the accident was given to the respondent No.2.
Even there are no documents before this court to show that after the accident the respondent No.1 being the employer has paid any amount to the petitioner towards medical expenses.
17. The initial burden is on the workmen to prove that the accident has took place during the course of employment and if he discharged the said burden then the burden shift on the employer.
In the instant case it is not under dispute that the petitioner was the employee under the respondent No.1 and he had sustained injuries during the course of employment.
Sri.Suresh Ananta Pujari @ Suresh vs Sri.A.Sreenivasulu Naidu

Further the petitioner has got examined the doctor as PW.2 who had stated that the petitioner has sustained compound communited fracture both bones left leg with loss of skin.
The petitioner had underwent skin grafting and external fixation for both bones fracture.
Later the external fixation was removed.
On examination it is noticed that the petitioner has restriction of joint movements of left knee.
Hence the PW.2 has assessed physical disability at 36% of left lower limb and 18% to whole body.

The PW.2 had got SCH3 10 E.C.A.No.36/2021 marked the OPD book and Xray as per Ex.P.11 and 12.
19.
Further the PW.2 in his cross examination has admitted that "It is true that I have assessed the disability after 05 years of accident.
That the fractures are malunited.

It is true that the implants are removed".
20.
Hence as per the oral evidence of PW.2, I just feel it proper to arrive to the conclusion that there is disability to the petitioner, but not as stated by the PW.2.
Even the PW.2 has not taken 1/3rd of whole body disability.
Hence under these circumstances I just feel it proper to fix 10% disability for whole body.
21. The petitioner himself stated that he was paying Rs.15,000/ p.m as salary and Rs.100/ as batta.
But he had not produced any documents in this regard.
As per the recent guidelines of the Government it is just and proper to fix Rs.15,000/ p.m as salary of the petitioner.
22. Therefore 60% of the income of the petitioner has to be considered for calculating compensation which comes to Rs.9,000/ p.m.
The petitioner in order to prove his age has got marked the driving licence as per Ex.P.8 which shows that he was SCH3 11 E.C.A.No.36/2021 born in the year 1978.
As per Ex.P.8 the age of the petitioner at the time of accident was 39 years.
Hence the applicable factor is "186.90"

Hence the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.9,000 x 186.90 = Rs.16,82,100/
.
Then Rs.16,82,100 x 10/100 = Rs.1,68,210/ payable by the respondent No.2 the insurer.
23. Further the petitioner has stated that he has incurred amount towards his medical expenses.
In this regard the PW.1 has got examined the Manager, Hillside hospital as PW.3 who has stated that the petitioner had took treatment in their hospital.
The PW.3 had also got marked inpatient bill and inpatient record as per Ex.P.14 and 15 which amounts to Rs.1,59,006/.
Even the PW.1 has got marked entire medical bills and prescriptions as per Ex.P.9 and 10 which comes to Rs.27,866/.
On perusal of Medical bills at Ex.P.9, it is noticed that Sl. No.72 is the receipt for credit bill amount of Rs.732/ at Sl. No.69, hence the said amount is not considered.
Thus the petitioner is entitled for Rs.1,86,140/ towards medical expenses payable by the respondent No.1 the employer.

Hence the petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.3,54,350/ SCH3 12 E.C.A.No.36/2021 (Three lakhs fifty four thousand three hundred and fifty only).
24.
Regarding liability:- There is no dispute that the respondent No.1 is the owner of the bus which is duly with the respondent No.2 on the date of accident.
Further it is true that the accident occurred and the petitioner has sustained injuries during the course of employment.

It is also true that still Sri.Suresh Ananta Pujari @ Suresh vs Sri.A.Sreenivasulu Naidu on 17 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6372059/
5 the petitioner has not received any compensation.

sentences.text: Therefore the petitioner is entitled for the compensation of Rs.3,54,350/ (Three lakhs fifty four thousand three hundred and fifty only).
But the petitioner is not entiteld for the interest and penalty payable by the insurance company.
It is true that the respondent No.2 have not produced the copy of policy but in these kind of cases the insurer are exempted from payment of interest and penalty.
Hence I answered the issue No.2 in partly affirmative.

25. Issue No.3: In view of my above finding, I proceed to pass the following :
ORDER Petition filed by the petitioner is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioner is totally entitled for Rs.3,54,350/
(Three lakhs fifty four thousand three hundred and fifty only) payable by both respondents No.1 and 2.
Out of the said amount the respondent No.1 being the employer is liable to pay a sum of Rs.1,86,140/ (One lakh eighty six thousand one hundred and forty only) to the petitioner and the respondent No.2 being the insurer are liable to pay the remaining amount i.e Rs.1,68,210/ (One lakh sixty eight thousand two hundred and ten only)
to the petitioner within two months from the date of this order to the tribunal's account directly through NEFT or RTGS as per the directions of Honorable High court of Karnataka vide General Circular No.2/2019

. 
On deposit of the compensation amount with interest, entire amount shall be released in the name of petitioner through Epayment on proper identification without any further proceedings.
The amount awarded if deposited, shall not be released till expiry of appeal period.

However before drawing the award, office is directed to obtain the Bank account details with IFSC code, along with front page of passbook with photograph of petitioners, pan card and aadhar card SCH3 14 E.C.A.No.36/2021 copies as per directions in General circular No.2/2019 and then proceed to draw award.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/ Draw award accordingly.
